results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that attests to an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a cryptographic integrity hash (SHA-256) and is anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps so its existence at a given moment can be proven independently. 

Anyone can verify a certificate for free using its QR code or by tapping an Attesté NFC tag on the artwork. The public view shows only the details the certificate holder chose to make verifiable, keeping private collection data secure.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A source certificate is a tamper-evident digital record issued directly by you as the artist from your studio at the point of creation. It records your own statement and acts as the genesis record for the artwork, carrying a cryptographic SHA-256 fingerprint anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps so its existence can be independently verified.

It is different from certificates issued later because it starts the provenance chain at your hand rather than reconstructing history years later from whatever paper survives. When a work leaves your studio with a source certificate, its story begins with you—establishing an authoritative first witness that travels with the work for life and serves as the foundation every later link builds on.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the very first record in an artwork’s provenance chain—made by the artist, in their own voice, at the exact moment of creation. 

When you register a new work on Attesté in your studio, you record its story yourself. That account is then sealed with a SHA-256 fingerprint and anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps. This creates an unchangeable origin story—provenance written forward rather than reconstructed years later from whatever paper survives—providing the strongest possible starting point that every later link builds upon.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
A physical NFC tag can be bound directly to an artwork's certificate of attestation. Once the tag is bound, you simply hold your phone against it to open that certificate's verification view — creating a physical handshake between the artwork on the wall and its digital provenance. 

To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app or use the scan action on a certificate, then hold the top of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. The linked certificate will then open automatically. Note that scanning NFC tags requires the iOS or Android app, as the web version cannot scan tags.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté uses AI across the platform to help you document, discover, and manage art without the heavy lifting. 

For collectors, the AI can identify an artwork from a photo (naming the artist, medium, and period), draft condition assessments, and power the AI Sommelier, which learns your taste profile across eight axes to recommend exhibitions and discoveries. You can also talk to the Atelier—a voice-and-camera assistant that sees what you see through your phone's camera, answers questions about style and technique, and saves journal entries directly to your artwork records.

For artists, the Atelier and Curator can draft descriptions, medium details, style tags, and artist bios from your photos and notes. For galleries, the Almanac AI concierge answers questions grounded in your live inventory and exhibitions, while AI writers draft exhibition copy, press releases, artwork descriptions, follow-up messages, and social media posts.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/ai-features, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/galleries

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account directly inside the app. Open your Profile and go to Settings, scroll down to Account, and tap Delete account. Type DELETE in exact capital letters to confirm, and tap the delete button. Your account and related records are removed server-side immediately. 

If you cannot access the app, you can also email info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account," and we will complete your request within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). Please note that deleting your account does not automatically cancel any active store subscription, so you will need to cancel that through your Apple ID or Google Play settings as well.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté offers a mobile-first experience with a genuine free tier (Explorer—25 works, no card required) and built-in AI assistants like Atelier for voice-and-camera work, identification, and condition documentation. It also anchors provenance using SHA-256 cryptographic hashes and Bitcoin timestamps, with certificates created at the moment of origin. 

Artwork Archive has been on the market since 2010 and is web-only with no native mobile app. It includes mature consignment management, a Discovery marketplace with a Call for Entry board, and a public profile with embeddable pages, but it has no AI features and offers a 14-day trial instead of a permanently free plan.

For collectors, Attesté's unlimited tier is $19.99/month, whereas Artwork Archive's top collector plan runs roughly $36–42/month. However, Artwork Archive remains a stronger choice if you need robust consignment-heavy gallery workflows, a built-in public marketplace, or a platform with a 15-year track record.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-vs-art-galleria
